name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.infinityCharacter
title: The scalar character of the unitization

content.display_title: The scalar character of the unitization
content.one_sentence_role: Names the character which reads the scalar coordinate and annihilates the embedded original algebra.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed. Write its complex unitization as $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$, with elements $(\lambda,a)$ and inclusion $\iota(a)=(0,a)$. The scalar character is a character of $\widetilde A$.
content.definition_explanation: Multiplication in the unitization is given by $(\lambda,a)(\mu,b)=(\lambda\mu,\lambda b+\mu a+ab)$. Thus $$\chi_\infty:\widetilde A\to\mathbb C,\qquad\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$$ is a complex algebra homomorphism with $\chi_\infty(1,0)=1$, hence a nonzero character. The RHS below presents this very scalar-coordinate homomorphism as an element of the character space.
content.assumptions: There is no nontriviality, order, separability, or representation-space hypothesis in this definition.
content.conclusion: The resulting character satisfies $\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$, and consequently $\chi_\infty(\iota(a))=0$ for every $a\in A$.
lean_realization_notes: For a closed unital $*$-subalgebra $D\subseteq\widetilde A$, the separate definition `infinityCharacterOn D` is its restriction $\chi_\infty|_D$. It is not a new character of $A$.
